title: KB-GRAPH-3: graph-freshness sensor — fail the gate when a done task has no task-<n> graph node
description:
From the 2026-07-18 intake+KB-graph design review (Q2, recommended path step 3). Nothing keeps knowledge/graph/graph.json synced to tasks/; the graph is already drifting — task nodes stop at task-150 while TASK-160..167 exist on disk. The manual write-at-close protocol is convention, not code. Add a lightweight sensor (in the style of dist-parity / use-case-policy) that fails test:all when a done ticket in tasks/ has no corresponding task-<digits> node in graph.json, converting silent drift into a caught defect.

NOTE: landing this sensor green requires BACKFILLING the currently-missing task nodes for already-done tickets (task-151..167 and any others) so main is green — include that backfill in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A sensor spec fails when a tasks/ ticket with status 'done' has no task-<digits> node in knowledge/graph/graph.json, naming the missing ticket key(s).
The sensor passes when every done ticket has a node; todo/in_progress/blocked/in_review tickets are NOT required to have nodes (only done).
The sensor is red-green planted: proven to fail on a seeded drift fixture and pass when the node is present.
The sensor runs within test:all (release gate) and is documented in the CLAUDE.md testing/sensor list (parity if a doc-lock applies).
As part of landing, the currently-missing task nodes for already-done tickets are backfilled so the sensor is GREEN on main at merge.
